summary: The Generic backend (module `grackle-generic`, package `grackle.generic`) lets you serve a GraphQL schema directly from ordinary Scala ADTs (case classes and sealed traits) without writing per-field mappings. Its core abstraction is the typeclass `CursorBuilder[T]`, which knows how to build a Grackle `Cursor` over a value of type `T`; instances for primitives, `Option`, `List`, Scala `Enumeration` values and any Circe-`Encoder` leaf are provided implicitly, and instances for product types (objects) and coproduct types (interfaces/unions) are derived semi-automatically via `semiauto.deriveObjectCursorBuilder` / `deriveInterfaceCursorBuilder` (shapeless on Scala 2, shapeless3 on Scala 3). A `GenericMapping[F]` wires these builders into the rest of Grackle by exposing `GenericField(fieldName, value)` field mappings and a `genericCursor` helper. There is no `@GraphQLField` or any other annotation in this codebase — derivation is purely structural (case-class field names must match GraphQL field names, and customisation is done explicitly with `renameField`/`transformFieldNames`/`transformField`).

keyConcepts.name: CursorBuilder[T] typeclass
keyConcepts.explanation: The central abstraction (modules/generic/src/main/scala/CursorBuilder.scala). A CursorBuilder[T] carries the GraphQL `tpe: Type` it produces and a `build(context, focus, parent, env): Result[Cursor]` method. Everything in the generic backend is about obtaining a CursorBuilder for your domain types. Summon one with `CursorBuilder[T]` (the apply on the companion).

keyConcepts.name: Implicit leaf/collection builders
keyConcepts.explanation: CursorBuilder.scala provides implicit instances for String, Int, Long, Float, Double, Boolean (PrimitiveCursor-backed leaves), `Option[T]` (nullable), `List[T]` (list), Scala `Enumeration#Value` (serialised via toString), and a fallback `leafCursorBuilder[T]` for any type with a Circe `Encoder[T]`. These are resolved automatically when deriving products/coproducts, so each field type must have a CursorBuilder in scope.

keyConcepts.name: Semiauto product derivation (objects)
keyConcepts.explanation: `semiauto.deriveObjectCursorBuilder[T](tpe)` derives an ObjectCursorBuilder[T] for a case class, mapping each case-class field name to a sub-CursorBuilder resolved for that field's type. The GraphQL object type is supplied explicitly as `tpe` (a schema.ref). Field names are matched structurally to the case-class member names.

keyConcepts.name: Semiauto coproduct derivation (interfaces/unions)
keyConcepts.explanation: `semiauto.deriveInterfaceCursorBuilder[T](tpe)` derives a CursorBuilder[T] for a sealed trait / sealed ADT whose subtypes each already have a CursorBuilder. At runtime it selects the concrete branch, builds with that branch's builder, and wraps it so the cursor reports the interface type but can `narrow` to the concrete subtype. Used for GraphQL `interface` (and union) types.

keyConcepts.name: GenericField mapping
keyConcepts.explanation: `GenericField(fieldName, value)` (defined in GenericMappingLike) is a FieldMapping that attaches a Scala value plus its implicit CursorBuilder to a schema field — typically used on the root Query ObjectMapping to expose the in-memory data. `subtree` is true and it can be `hidden`. GenericMapping overrides `mkCursorForMappedField` to dispatch GenericField to its builder.

keyConcepts.name: Field customisation combinators
keyConcepts.explanation: ObjectCursorBuilder[T] adds `renameField(from, to)`, `transformFieldNames(f)`, and `transformField[U](name)(f: T => Result[U])`. transformField is the key escape hatch: it replaces a derived field with a computed/effect-free resolution (e.g. resolving foreign-key id lists to nested objects), which is also how recursion between types is broken.

keyConcepts.name: Recursion via lazy/by-name builders
keyConcepts.explanation: CursorBuilder implicit parameters are taken by-name (`implicit cb: => CursorBuilder[T]`), GenericField stores a `() => CursorBuilder[T]` thunk, and Impl's fieldMap is a lazy `=> FieldMap[T]`. This laziness lets mutually-recursive types (Programme <-> Production) and self-referential graphs define their builders as implicit vals without initialization-order deadlock.

keyConcepts.name: genericCursor / DeferredCursor
keyConcepts.explanation: `genericCursor(path, env, t)` builds a Cursor for a value at an arbitrary path: at the root it builds eagerly; otherwise it returns a `DeferredCursor` that defers building until the surrounding context/parent is known. This is what you return from a RootEffect.computeCursor to plug a generic value into the effectful root.

keyTypes.name: CursorBuilder[T]
keyTypes.purpose: Core typeclass: knows the GraphQL Type and how to build a Cursor over a T. contramap adapts an existing builder to a wrapper type (e.g. CursorBuilder[String].contramap(_.value) for a single-field value class).

keyTypes.name: CursorBuilder.apply
keyTypes.signature: def apply[T](implicit cb: CursorBuilder[T]): CursorBuilder[T] = cb
keyTypes.purpose: Summoner used in tests/examples as CursorBuilder[T] to obtain the in-scope instance.

keyTypes.name: deriveLeafCursorBuilder
keyTypes.signature: def deriveLeafCursorBuilder[T](tpe0: Type)(implicit encoder: Encoder[T]): CursorBuilder[T]
keyTypes.purpose: Builds a leaf CursorBuilder for a custom scalar type given a Circe Encoder and the GraphQL scalar Type (e.g. CursorBuilder.deriveLeafCursorBuilder[Genre](GenreType)).

keyTypes.name: leafCursorBuilder (implicit)
keyTypes.signature: implicit def leafCursorBuilder[T](implicit encoder: Encoder[T]): CursorBuilder[T] = deriveLeafCursorBuilder(StringType)
keyTypes.purpose: Implicit fallback: any T with a Circe Encoder becomes a leaf cursor reporting StringType. Drives the java.time / UUID scalar examples (their Encoders come from io.circe).

keyTypes.name: deriveEnumerationCursorBuilder / enumerationCursorBuilder
keyTypes.signature:
def deriveEnumerationCursorBuilder[T <: Enumeration#Value](tpe0: Type): CursorBuilder[T]
implicit def enumerationCursorBuilder[T <: Enumeration#Value]: CursorBuilder[T] = deriveEnumerationCursorBuilder(StringType)
keyTypes.purpose: Serialises a Scala Enumeration value as its .toString. Implicit version reports StringType.

keyTypes.name: optionCursorBuiler / listCursorBuiler (implicit)
keyTypes.signature:
implicit def optionCursorBuiler[T](implicit elemBuilder: CursorBuilder[T]): CursorBuilder[Option[T]]
implicit def listCursorBuiler[T](implicit elemBuilder: CursorBuilder[T]): CursorBuilder[List[T]]
keyTypes.purpose: Nullable and list wrappers (note the misspelled 'Builer' in both method names — they are public). Option => NullableType, List => ListType.

keyTypes.name: GenericMapping[F]
keyTypes.signature: abstract class GenericMapping[F[_]](implicit val M: MonadThrow[F]) extends Mapping[F] with GenericMappingLike[F]
keyTypes.purpose: Base class your mapping object/trait extends to use generic derivation. Requires a MonadThrow[F].

keyTypes.name: GenericMappingLike[F].genericCursor
keyTypes.signature: def genericCursor[T](path: Path, env: Env, t: T)(implicit cb: => CursorBuilder[T]): Result[Cursor]
keyTypes.purpose: Builds a (possibly deferred) Cursor for a value t at path; used inside RootEffect.computeCursor to produce an effect-specific generic cursor.

keyTypes.name: GenericField (case class + factory)
keyTypes.signature:
case class GenericField[T](val fieldName: String, t: T, cb: () => CursorBuilder[T], hidden: Boolean)(implicit val pos: SourcePos) extends FieldMapping { def subtree: Boolean = true }

def GenericField[T](fieldName: String, t: T, hidden: Boolean = false)(implicit cb: => CursorBuilder[T], pos: SourcePos): GenericField[T]
keyTypes.purpose: FieldMapping that exposes a Scala value (plus its by-name CursorBuilder) at a schema field. The factory is the normal entry point; cb is captured as a thunk for recursion safety.

keyTypes.name: semiauto.deriveObjectCursorBuilder
keyTypes.signature: final def deriveObjectCursorBuilder[T](tpe: Type)(implicit mkBuilder: => MkObjectCursorBuilder[T]): ObjectCursorBuilder[T]
keyTypes.purpose: Derives an object (GraphQL type) CursorBuilder for a case class T mapped to schema type tpe.

keyTypes.name: semiauto.deriveInterfaceCursorBuilder
keyTypes.signature: final def deriveInterfaceCursorBuilder[T](tpe: Type)(implicit mkBuilder: => MkInterfaceCursorBuilder[T]): CursorBuilder[T]
keyTypes.purpose: Derives an interface/union CursorBuilder for a sealed trait T mapped to schema type tpe; produced cursor narrows to concrete subtypes.

keyTypes.name: ObjectCursorBuilder[T]
keyTypes.purpose: Customisation surface returned by deriveObjectCursorBuilder: rename fields and replace a derived field with a computed Result[U].

keyTypes.name: MkObjectCursorBuilder / productCursorBuilder (Scala 3)
keyTypes.signature:
trait MkObjectCursorBuilder[T] { def apply(tpe: Type): ObjectCursorBuilder[T] }
implicit def productCursorBuilder[T <: Product](implicit inst: K0.ProductInstances[CursorBuilder, T], labelling: Labelling[T]): MkObjectCursorBuilder[T]
keyTypes.purpose: Scala 3 (shapeless3) derivation of the object builder; uses Labelling for field names and ProductInstances to project each field.

keyTypes.name: MkInterfaceCursorBuilder / coproductCursorBuilder (Scala 3)
keyTypes.signature:
trait MkInterfaceCursorBuilder[T] { def apply(tpe: Type): CursorBuilder[T] }
implicit def coproductCursorBuilder[T](implicit inst: => K0.CoproductInstances[CursorBuilder, T]): MkInterfaceCursorBuilder[T]
keyTypes.purpose: Scala 3 derivation of the interface/union builder via CoproductInstances.fold.

keyTypes.name: MkObjectCursorBuilder / productCursorBuilder (Scala 2)
keyTypes.signature: implicit def productCursorBuilder[T <: Product, R <: HList, L <: HList](implicit gen: Generic.Aux[T, R], elems0: => PLiftAll[CursorBuilder, R], lgen: LabelledGeneric.Aux[T, L], keys0: Keys[L]): MkObjectCursorBuilder[T]
keyTypes.purpose: Scala 2 (shapeless) equivalent: derives field map from LabelledGeneric record keys and per-field CursorBuilder instances.

keyTypes.name: MkInterfaceCursorBuilder / coproductCursorBuilder (Scala 2)
keyTypes.signature: implicit def coproductCursorBuilder[T, R <: Coproduct](implicit gen: Generic.Aux[T, R], elems0: => CLiftAll[CursorBuilder, R]): MkInterfaceCursorBuilder[T]
keyTypes.purpose: Scala 2 equivalent for sealed-trait coproducts; selects the branch index by walking the Coproduct.

minimalExamples.title: Derive an object CursorBuilder for a case class
minimalExamples.explanation: Minimal object derivation, taken from EffectsSuite.scala. The case class fields n: Int and s: String resolve to the implicit Int/String CursorBuilders automatically. The GraphQL type is passed explicitly.

minimalExamples.title: Sealed trait as a GraphQL interface, with per-subtype objects
minimalExamples.explanation: From the demo (demo/src/main/scala/demo/starwars/StarWarsMapping.scala) and DerivationSuite.scala. The interface builder over the sealed trait dispatches to each subtype's object builder and supports `narrow` to Human/Droid for `... on Human` fragments. transformField replaces the derived `friends` (a List[String] of ids) with resolved nested Characters.

minimalExamples.title: transformField to resolve a foreign-key list to nested objects
minimalExamples.explanation: From DerivationSuite.scala / demo. The derived field has a different Scala shape than the GraphQL field; transformField[U] supplies a T => Result[U] and the implicit CursorBuilder[U] (here CursorBuilder[Option[List[Character]]]) is summoned to build the replacement cursor.

minimalExamples.title: Custom scalar leaf via Circe Encoder + deriveLeafCursorBuilder
minimalExamples.explanation: From ScalarsSuite.scala. java.time and UUID fields work through the implicit leafCursorBuilder (they have Circe Encoders); the Genre enum-like ADT is given an explicit leaf builder bound to the GraphQL scalar GenreType. Note these are LEAF scalars, not coproduct-derived objects.

minimalExamples.title: Wire generic builders into a Mapping with GenericField
minimalExamples.explanation: From DerivationSuite.scala. GenericField(name, value) exposes the in-memory data at the root; the implicit CursorBuilder for the value's type (List[Character], List[Human], ...) is picked up automatically. A SelectElaborator then narrows the list with Unique/Filter/Eql.

minimalExamples.title: Effectful root cursor with genericCursor + RootEffect.computeCursor
minimalExamples.explanation: From EffectsSuite.scala. RootEffect.computeCursor runs an effect (here bumping a Ref) and yields a Result[Cursor] built by genericCursor(path, env, value), which defers cursor construction until the field context is known.

minimalExamples.title: Mutually recursive types via transformField
minimalExamples.explanation: From RecursionSuite.scala. Programme references Production and vice-versa. Storing ids (String) in the model and resolving them in transformField breaks the cycle; the by-name implicit CursorBuilder parameters mean the two implicit vals can refer to each other without initialization errors.

gotchas: There is NO @GraphQLField (or any) annotation in the generic backend — derivation is purely structural. The case-class field NAME must exactly match the GraphQL field name; to differ, use renameField/transformFieldNames. The FOCUS hint about @GraphQLField does not apply to this codebase.

The GraphQL Type is always passed explicitly to deriveObjectCursorBuilder[T](tpe) / deriveInterfaceCursorBuilder[T](tpe) / deriveLeafCursorBuilder[T](tpe). Nothing is inferred from the Scala type name; a mismatch between case-class fields and the schema type's fields is only caught at query time (e.g. 'No field ...').

Implicit method names are misspelled: optionCursorBuiler and listCursorBuiler (missing the 'd'). If you ever reference them by name (rather than relying on implicit resolution) you must use the typo'd spelling.
Long maps to IntType and Double/Float both map to FloatType in the primitive builders (CursorBuilder.scala). There is no separate GraphQL type for Long/Double — they share Int/Float.

leafCursorBuilder is an implicit fallback for ANY type with a Circe Encoder and it reports StringType. This means a domain type with an Encoder in scope will silently be treated as a String leaf even where you intended an object — and it can shadow/compete with object derivation. Custom scalars rely on this (java.time, UUID, Genre).

CursorBuilder implicits are by-name (=> CursorBuilder[T]) and GenericField captures a () => CursorBuilder[T] thunk; Impl.fieldMap is lazy. This is deliberate for recursion. If you eagerly force a builder during construction of a mutually-recursive pair you can reintroduce initialization-order problems.

Recursion between object types is NOT automatic from the ADT shape — RecursionSuite models references as id Strings and resolves them with transformField. A naive directly-recursive case class (holding the related object) would require the related type's CursorBuilder to exist, which the by-name machinery allows, but the test/demo pattern is id-plus-resolver.

transformField's replacement type U must have its own CursorBuilder in scope (the implicit cb: => CursorBuilder[U] parameter). For resolveFriends returning Result[Option[List[Character]]] this means CursorBuilder[Option[List[Character]]] (via the Option/List/interface builders) must resolve.

The interface/union cursor wraps the concrete branch's cursor; narrow only succeeds when subtpe <:< interfaceTpe AND concreteTpe <:< subtpe (CursorImpl.narrowsTo). Querying a subtype-only field without a matching fragment, or narrowing to an unrelated type, yields an internalError 'cannot be narrowed'.

Scala 2 vs Scala 3 use different derivation engines (shapeless vs shapeless3) in separate source roots (scala-2/genericmapping2.scala, scala-3/genericmapping3.scala) but expose the identical public surface (MkObjectCursorBuilder/MkInterfaceCursorBuilder/ObjectCursorBuilder). Don't document shapeless-specific implicits (Generic.Aux, K0.ProductInstances) as public API — they are derivation internals.

GenericMapping requires an implicit MonadThrow[F]; the in-memory examples use IO. Fields resolved purely from data don't run effects, but RootEffect.computeCursor + genericCursor is the path for effectful roots.
